standard.title: Arts importance for communities
standard.description: explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students bring lived experience of arts in daily life (songs, drawings, stories, celebrations) but have not yet been invited to reflect on why arts matter to communities.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify examples of arts in their lives and communities and share ideas about why arts are important for people and communities.

nodes.label: Identifying arts in daily life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify arts works and experiences in their own lives — naming songs, artworks, dances, animations or performances they know.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least one arts work or experience from their own life (a song, a drawing, a dance).
nodes.typical_width: Identify arts works and experiences across multiple forms (visual, music, dance, drama, digital) encountered at school, at home and in community settings.
wider: Identify arts works from different cultural celebrations (school songs, ceremonial dances, birthday traditions) — compare which forms appear in different communities
Use dramatic play to explore a text or image — act out 'what is happening?' and 'what will happen next?' to understand how arts communicate story
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify arts in their own lives have no foundation from which to reason about why arts matter — the subsequent conceptual move (importance) requires concrete examples to anchor it.

response_modes.reason: Students need a sufficient inventory of examples before they can generalise about why arts matter. Broadening the range of recognised arts forms ensures the concept applies beyond a single familiar type.

success_criteria: Names at least one arts work or experience from their own life
Can categorise it as visual art, music, dance, drama or digital

nodes.label: Why arts matter to people
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share an idea about why an arts work or experience is important — connecting it to feelings, celebrations, stories or communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one idea about why a specific arts work matters to them or their community (e.g. it makes people happy, it tells a story, it is used in celebrations).
nodes.typical_width: Explore how arts works communicate emotions, stories and cultural meanings; discuss why different arts forms matter to different people and communities.
wider: Listen to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of arts for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place — using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians
Explore how illustrations in a picture book communicate narrative and mood — discuss how the visual choices help the story and why that matters to readers

response_modes.reason: Students' initial reasons why arts matter are usually personal ('I like it'). Encountering arts that matter to different communities — especially First Nations voices — broadens understanding beyond personal preference.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations perspectives on the arts as connection to Country/Place and culture provide genuinely different reasoning about importance — moving students from personal preference to community and cultural function.
success_criteria: Shares at least one reason why an arts work matters to them or their community
Connects the reason to feelings, celebrations, stories or communication (not just 'I like it')

nodes.label: Arts in communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore how and why arts are important for people and communities — identifying examples and explaining their importance in terms of shared meaning, celebration or connection.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of arts that is shared by or important to a community (not just an individual) and explain why.
nodes.typical_width: Explore arts works and events that are important to communities — songs, public art, cultural celebrations, shared stories; discuss the role arts play in bringing people together and communicating shared values.
wider: Investigate arts works that serve specific community functions (school songs, sports team anthems, ceremonial dances) — compare different communities' arts traditions
Explore how facial expressions, gesture and visual imagery communicate feelings across cultures — discuss how this shared function makes arts important everywhere

response_modes.reason: Students bring together their personal examples and their understanding of why arts matter to arrive at the broader claim: arts are important for communities, not just individuals.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one example of arts important to a community (not just an individual)
Explains why the arts work or event matters to that community
